name: CVRP X-n895-k37
description: Route identical vehicles of capacity 1816 from one depot to serve the 894 customers of the CVRPLIB X-set instance X-n895-k37. Every customer is visited exactly once, the total demand on a route may not exceed the capacity, and every route starts and ends at the depot. The number of routes is free (the k in the instance name does not limit it). Minimise the total cost: the sum over all routes of the Euclidean distances between consecutive stops, the legs from and to the depot included, each distance rounded to the nearest integer.

sources.locator: Hybrid genetic search for the CVRP: Open-source implementation and SWAP* neighborhood

CVRPLIB instance table: X-n895-k37 (customers, vehicle capacity, best known solution, optimality column), the instance file and the set conventions (Euclidean distance rounded to the nearest integer, total distance as cost, number of routes free).
CVRPLIB update log (7 pages, read in full): dated entries naming who reported each improved best known solution of X-n895-k37 and with which method.

Uchoa, Pecin, Pessoa, Poggi, Vidal and Subramanian (2017), New benchmark instances for the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (Crossref: European Journal of Operational Research, March 2017): the X instance set, its generator and attributes; a benchmark paper, so not counted as evidence.

requirements.datasets: CVRPLIB X instance file X-n895-k37.vrp (galgos.inf.puc-rio.br/cvrplib, download/instance/id)

execution.interface: solve(inst) -> list of routes; a route is a list of customer ids from 1 to n in visiting order (the depot is node 0 and is not listed; empty routes are ignored). inst is a dict with n (number of customers), capacity, coords (array of shape (n + 1, 2), row 0 is the depot), demand (integer array of length n + 1, demand[0] = 0) and name. Score: the total cost, minimized.

science_relevance.reason: The cited paper poses the capacitated vehicle routing problem that the evaluator scores exactly on the pinned CVRPLIB X instance; where CVRPLIB credits a best known solution to a method paper, an override adds that paper, and the instance-set paper stays under extra_sources.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find a minimum-cost set of capacity-feasible vehicle routes from one depot that serves every customer of the CVRPLIB X instance X-n895-k37.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: The capacitated vehicle routing problem is the core model of distribution logistics (delivery, collection and service fleets). It is NP-hard; the X instances of 100 to 1,000 customers were generated to cover the attributes that make it hard, and the 39 that CVRPLIB lists as not proven optimal are open, so a cheaper set of routes is a new best known solution of an open standard instance.

papers.title: The Truck Dispatching Problem
papers.task_relation: The task's objective is the capacitated vehicle routing cost (rounded Euclidean distances, free number of routes) on the fixed CVRPLIB instance X-n895-k37.
papers.primary_goal: Formulate and solve the routing of a fleet of capacitated trucks from a terminal to service stations, introducing the capacitated vehicle routing problem.

papers.title: Hybrid genetic search for the CVRP: Open-source implementation and SWAP* neighborhood
papers.task_relation: The CVRPLIB update log of 25 Oct 2026 credits the current best known solution of X-n895-k37 to Christoph Breunig, who started from the published solution and re-solved subsets of routes with HGS-CVRP (Vidal 2022); this is the HGS-CVRP paper, and the task asks for a cost below that value.
papers.primary_goal: Present an open-source hybrid genetic search for the capacitated vehicle routing problem with the SWAP* neighbourhood and show that it improves the state of the art on CVRP benchmark instances.
